Work expands to fill the time allotted, with decreasing marginal returns.

Machines doing too many of the tasks means loss of the particular job in question.

Controlling for quality of the thing, cheaper things get used more, and total amount paid can go up or go down.

Labor is paid well if and only if it is the scarce resource, which it may not be.

trace.research:
The core assertion — that Czechoslovakia ended up with a comparatively LARGE remaining Jewish population — is contradicted by standard Holocaust demography. USHMM's country-by-country losses list a 1921/1930 Czechoslovak Jewish population of ~354,000 with ~260,000 deaths, including Bohemia-Moravia 117,551 with 77,297 deaths, Slovakia 88,951 (1940) with ~60,000 deaths, and Hungarian-annexed southern Slovakia/Subcarpathian Rus 142,000–148,000 with 114,000–120,000 deaths (https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/jewish-losses-during-the-holocaust-by-country). USHMM elsewhere states ~263,000 Jews who lived on 1938 Czechoslovak territory were killed (https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/the-holocaust-in-bohemia-and-moravia). The Czech-lands community was 'virtually annihilated': of a pre-invasion 118,310, about 14,000 remained by 1945/1946 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Holocaust_in_Bohemia_and_Moravia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Czechoslovakia); the US National Archives says ~10,000 of nearly 120,000 Bohemia-Moravia Jews survived (https://www.archives.gov/research/holocaust/finding-aid/civilian/rg-84-czech.html). For Slovakia, 68,000–71,000 (~80% of the pre-war population) were murdered (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_exemption_(Slovak_State)); the State Department notes 57,000 deported March–October 1942 with only a few hundred survivors (https://www.state.gov/reports/just-act-report-to-congress/slovakia). Czechoslovakia's postwar Jewish population fell from 356,830 (1930) to ~55,000 in 1946, an ~85% drop (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Czechoslovakia). That survival rate is among Europe's worst — far below France (300,000–330,000 with 72,900–74,000 deaths), Italy (~7,858 deaths of ~43,000 under German occupation), and Denmark (7,500 with 52–116 deaths) per the same USHMM table. Today's numbers likewise do not support the claim: ~3,900 Jews in the Czech Republic and ~2,600 in Slovakia versus, e.g., Hungary ~47,900 and France ~438,500 (https://www.worldjewishcongress.org/en/about/communities/CZ, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_population_by_country).

The kernel of truth is narrow and concerns wartime Slovakia (an Axis client state, not a Nazi-occupied country): 'exemption certificates' (výnimky) were issued in 1942 to Jews deemed economically essential (https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/pinkas_slovakia/slo588.html), and Tiso's presidential exemptions were 'granted to highly trained professionals such as doctors who were valuable to the Slovak war effort' — but only about 600 documented exemptions covering ~1,000 people, issued mostly after the 1942 deportations had already stopped and all nullified when Germany invaded in 1944 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_exemption_(Slovak_State)). A documented case is physician Rudolf Welward, exempted from the 1942 transports and again protected in 1944 by being made a camp doctor (https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/14623528.2025.2566566). So doctor exemptions existed and saved a small number of individuals, but they were a Slovak (not Nazi) policy affecting roughly a thousand people and did nothing to make Czechoslovakia's remaining Jewish population unusually large — the opposite is true.

“[These arguments] depend on the premises that humans are so gifted that they can design an omniscient and omnipotent AI” (source)

“They assumed that human engineers would grant [AIs] unlimited and irreversible control over the earth’s physical infrastructure, amounting to omnipotence over every atom on the planet.” (source)

“When we put aside fantasies like foom, digital megalomania, instant omniscience, and perfect control of every molecule in the universe…” (source)

“From animals to dull humans to smart humans to AI to Artificial Superintelligence, the latter consisting of perfect omniscience.” (source)

…and many more statements along the same lines.

Superintelligences are still bounded … They are (presumably) not infinitely smart, infinitely fast, all-knowing, or able to achieve every describable outcome using their available resources and options … A superintelligence doesn’t know everything and can’t perfectly estimate every quantity … A superintelligence is not omnipotent and can’t obtain every describable outcome.

Every definition of superintelligence, from Bostrom’s to Yudkowsky’s to Good’s, agrees that a superintelligence is merely a mind which is significantly smarter than any human’s.

Nor are we motte-and-baileying here, pretending we don’t think it’s omnipotent, but then treating it as omnipotent anyway. In the AI 2027 scenario, we state that superintelligence is achieved in late 2027 or early 2028, but that it’s unable to cleanly eliminate humans at that time, because it can’t maintain the data centers on its own. It takes two years of plotting before the superintelligence is able to finally eliminate humanity while preserving its own existence.

Where I think you are getting this is that we’re uncomfortable saying that superintelligence definitely can’t do any specific non-physically-impossible thing. For example, in the 2010s, we argued that people needed to be prepared for superintelligence designing dangerous biological weapons. Many people objected that this was absurd, because bioweapon design was bottlenecked on the protein folding problem, and there was no way that even superintelligence could solve protein folding. Then in 2020 one of Demis Hassabis’ narrow pre-LLM AIs solved protein folding easily. See also this this essay.

Gary Marcus is a cognitive scientist who spent the 2000s and 2010s pursuing a different road to AI that didn’t work out (hybrid neurosymbolics). He also has no expertise in modern LLMs. He is the person you retweeted in 2019 who was saying that deep learning had failed and would never amount to anything. He was also the person whose opinion you were affirming in 2022 when you said modern AI wouldn’t be able to do simple math. Yoshua Bengio, another Turing Award winning inventor of modern AI, also did that. Ilya Sutskever, the former Chief Scientist of OpenAI who helped invent ChatGPT and the modern LLM, wrote that superintelligence “could lead to the disempowerment of humanity or even human extinction”, and quit his job at OpenAI to found a company called Safe Superintelligence. AI Safety Is Mostly A Sex Cult In Berkeley, California
SE GYGES
3 HOURS AGO

These people shouldn’t make policy.

There has been a great effort over many years to distance AI Safety discussion from its origin and intellectual center, because its center is a predatory sex cult started by a fan fiction author. Since those involved want to be taken seriously, they have to hide that. Everyone else working in AI Safety is, effectively, a smokescreen for this core group and their ideas.

We might some day have “AI Safety”, as a science or policy area, that is not primarily a sex cult in Berkeley, California, but it does not currently exist.

Who Is Eliezer Yudkowsky?

This is Eliezer Yudkowsky. He is seen here in a meeting with Bernie Sanders, who he is advising on AI policy, and in The AI Doc, now on Netflix.

This is Yudkowsky in Time Magazine in 2023, advocating in favor of risking nuclear war to prevent AI research from happening anywhere on Earth.

This is very senior OpenAI employee and unofficial OpenAI spokesman Roon. Roon’s opinion of Yudkowsky is that:

Yudkowsky is in and/or running a sex cult.

Yudkowsky’s opinions about AI are important, and should be taken seriously.

This seems to be an extremely common pair of opinions concerning Yudkowsky.

Yudkowsky is sufficiently controversial that people motivated by his ideas often downplay or deny his influence. Sometimes this spans multiple layers: People who received money from Sam Bankman-Fried denying they’re Effective Altruists, Sam Bankman-Fried denying he’s an Effective Altruist when caught, Effective Altruists denying their version of AI Safety is heavily influenced by Yudkowsky’s, people literally attending the same orgies as Yudkowsky passing themselves off as merely “rationalist adjacent”, and so on. But Yudkowsky is provably, publicly influential on essentially all major public figures in AI. It is easy to deny not because it is hidden but because it seems so insane.

Yudkowsky is the person who connected Shane Legg and Demis Hassabis to Peter Thiel so that they could secure funding to start DeepMind1, which is now Google's AI research division. Here's Sam Altman's opinion of Yudkowsky.

This is the schedule for the Future of Life Institute's conference on AI in Puerto Rico in January, 2015. Elon Musk would found OpenAI that December. So it seems plausible that his attendance did influence the founding of OpenAI.

Dario Amodei, current CEO of Anthropic, is here in 2013 identified as a "member of the Effective Altruism community" on the blog of Yudkowsky's non-profit.

And here he is arguing about the paperclip maximizer, a now-classic thought experiment, originally Yudkowsky’s, about an AI that might kill everyone.

“AI Alignment” and “AI Safety” were first popularized by Yudkowsky’s non-profit, MIRI, the Machine Intelligence Research Institute. OpenAI and Anthropic have cited Yudkowsky or his non-profit at least a dozen times, and the entire way we talk about AI uses terminology his non-profit popularized. It is effectively impossible to even discuss these areas without, implicitly or explicitly, performing commentary on Yudkowsky’s writing.

This is Jacob Coxon, the recent “whistleblower” who quit Anthropic, being asked his opinions on rationalists and effective altruists.

This is Nate Silver citing LessWrong as a source of major information about AI risk. LessWrong is a website started by Yudkowsky in 2009, and originally filled only with his writing.

This is Oliver Habryka, who runs the nonprofit controlling LessWrong and the rationalist’s compound, known as Lighthaven, explaining how large he thinks the influence of rationalism is on AI Safety and AI existential risk discourse. He is engaged in some kind of internal territorial dispute here. It is possibly the only time I have ever agreed with him.

This is a podcast interview with Daniel Alejandro Moreno-Gama, who attempted to firebomb Sam Altman’s house, in which he names Yudkowsky as his primary influence.

Who Are The Rationalists?

Yudkowsky’s more dedicated followers seem to prefer to call themselves “the rationality community” these days, everyone else calls them “rationalists”, the entire following “rationalism”. I generally prefer “rats”.

This is a long denial that they are a religion. I alternate between finding it funny and finding it insulting.

The fan fiction that launched a thousand cults is Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality, or HPMOR. It is possibly the highest-impact single modern religious text, rivalled only by the Book of Mormon. Its influence may not yet have peaked. It is the holy book of the first great internet cult.

Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality
How Are Rationalists Connected To The Bay Area Effective Altruists?
Bay Area Effective Altruism meetup’s banner photo. Can you spot Yudkowsky?

Allegedly, Effective Altruism and its AI safety efforts are a separate thing and not directly beholden to Yudkowsky. This is fundamentally not true. Effective Altruism in the Bay Area has almost perfect overlap with rationalism, and the Effective Altruist AI Safety people in the Bay set the agenda for the rest of Effective Altruism’s safety efforts.

In the Bay Area, Rationalism and Effective Altruism are the same people, at the same events, in the same places, who believe the things said by the same authors and leaders, with only very slight differences between spheres of influence. Yudkowsky called himself an effective altruist and a rationalist until a peculiar internal schism. Scott Alexander, the second-most influential writer in the space, has usually called himself both. They generally work for the same companies and non-profits.

Frequently, Effective Altruists bring up all of Effective Altruism’s other charitable activities and its charming, benevolent members who don’t live in the Bay Area to deflect true criticisms of the Bay Area Effective Altruist community. This effectively makes their other charitable operations and workers shields and fronts for the priorities and behavior of the Effective Altruists in the Bay Area, who are interested almost exclusively in AI.

Where there is any separation between the two things in the Bay, “rationalism” is people and things more closely tied to Yudkowsky, and “effective altruism” has had a few institutional centers but is currently focused around Anthropic and its CEO, Dario Amodei. They compete for attention and funding in that space. Yudkowsky’s position is that AI will definitely kill us, and Dario’s position is that AI is ten to twenty-five percent likely to kill us.

Since Yudkowsky is a writer and not a scientist of any kind, he can only claim that he and his organization are important and deserve money and prestige if AI Safety is an unsolvable problem and only advocating against AI matters. Since Dario leads a company that actually makes AI, he must claim that AI doom is a very large problem that only his company can manage.

Yudkowsky also claimed that his (non-profit) company was probably the only one that could make AI safely, back when AI companies seldom made anything and he could claim to be doing research by simply writing. This belief system has been strenuously improved for, among other things, being a pitch to investors, donors, volunteers and employees. It is also a pitch for people to give you total control over them, because if they do not, the world might end. After Yudkowsky refined this pitch and mostly used it to form a sex cult, modifications of it became the pitch for organizations like OpenAI and Anthropic, and this is integral to employee morale and recruiting because so many research staff are believers to one degree or another.

Yudkowsky is not going to stop preaching the gospel of doom, among other reasons because he is effectively paid for it and it is the only job he has ever had. He would stand to lose his social position and the roughly 600k in income he is paid out of his non-profit if he changed his tune. In general, if doom prophecies are worth money, people will produce more. This system’s purpose is to attract funding and young idealists and to find ways to spend the funding and make use of the young idealists. One of the ways that young idealists are made use of is by using them for sex, or introducing them to sex work.

People tend to follow their incentives.

EA impact on Anthropic, on policy

Holden Karnofsky, Ben Mann, Daniela Amodei, Amanda Askell, and Jack Clark and Tom Brown are all Effective Altruists and have affiliated themselves with Effective Altruist pledges and causes.

Dario in particular is almost perfectly on-type for a Bay Area Effective Altruist in what he says and how he says it. Dario’s often bizarre, vague, and meandering writing style alone has no real precedent besides LessWrong and its AI-focused spinoff, Alignment Forum. Their company’s strategy is very close to the playbook Yudkowsky laid out, back before companies which were actually capable of doing science removed any credibility Yudkowsky’s organization had when it claimed to do AI research.

This same thing happens when it comes to the incestuous relationships between all of the other non-profits in the Bay that are meant to be focused on AI risk. They all have one of a few sources of funding and they recruit from the movement. Holden Karnofsky, currently Anthropic, formerly head of Coefficient Giving, was an original board member of Redwood Research and one of the initial champions for METR. Both are held up as independent organizations and are not. Redwood mostly seems to be trying to catch the same lightning in a bottle that Yudkowsky had with MIRI in inspiring devotion, to avoid behaving in any of the obviously disgraceful ways Yudkowsky is prone, and to launder essentially the same world view into policy papers that can be cited and pointed to as having come from a serious organization.

In the video with Bernie Sanders, the present people are:

Eliezer Yudkowsky, MIRI

Nate Soares, MIRI

Jeffrey Ladish (funded by Coefficient Giving, an EA charity)

Daniel Kokotajlo (funded by Survival and Flourishing Fund, an EA charity)

So when they go to get people to talk to a senator we have Yudkowsky, Yudkowsky’s top lieutenant, and two people whose paychecks are from Effective Altruist charities. We will be seeing three of these four again later.

Former Biden White House officials Bruce Reed and Ben Buchanan recently wrote an op-ed in which they deny having said that they wanted to ban open-source AI. They claim the first thing they were told in that meeting was to watch out for “the sex cult that wants to run America’s AI policy.”

They then deny being Effective Altruists.

Ben Buchanan worked for two years as Director of the CyberAI Project at Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET), which appears to have received roughly 90% of its funding from Coefficient Giving (then OpenPhilanthropy). Since May 2025, four months after the end of the Biden administration he has been working as a consultant for Anthropic.

Buchanan has a book, published March 2022, in which he discusses the possibility of export controlling GPUs. In October 2022, the Biden administration put in place export restrictions for GPUs.

I read Buchanan’s book2, and I think he is probably not an Effective Altruist because his ideas are not weird enough; but since 2019, his salary has come either from Effective Altruism or from the White House. I am reasonably sure he comes by his opinions honestly, and believes in them for normal policy advisor reasons. If he changes his opinions his career is probably in trouble.

Aligning a Smarter Than Human Intelligence is Difficult

Seth Lazar on The Construction of Moral Character in AIs. This was the biggest thing that jumped out:

Incoherent Values

Evaluating coherence is hard! Building on prior work, we have a new approach.

LLMs’ preferences over arbitrary statements are less coherent than previous research suggested; and may indicate failures of OOD [out of distribution] generalization of character.

… But that persona doesn’t necessarily generalize that much OOD. It may have coherent preferences on statements that are relatively close to the data that it was post-trained on, but for statements outside of that distribution, it reverts to the chaotic superposition of preferences that exists in the base model.

This would be very interesting if it proved to be true. One reason why Anthropic leans into the persona selection model of post-training is because these personas, or characters, are thought to generalize better than alternatives OOD. This may not be the case.​

If the character strategy is going to work, it needs to work OOD. A lot of this is a summary of prior work. The Blind Refusal result is interesting, where ChatGPT refuses to help you evade obviously stupid refusals but Claude and Gemini will often cooperate. This was covered briefly back in AI #164. The best humans in such spots will help you evade the rules.

Lazar suggests that we have ‘saturated’ textual moral sensitivity, because they do better at this than human philosophers, with the ability to filter out noise. I would say that these are two very different things, and there remains a long way to go even in theory, and also this does not translate so well to moral motivation, real-world perception or agent behavior.

The Warmth vs. Rigor axis contrasts values like positive framing and encouragement with values like accuracy and transparency.

The Depth vs. Brevity axis contrasts values like nuance and critical thinking with values like brevity and compliance.

The Candor vs. Execution axis contrasts values like honesty and transparency with values like results orientation and optimization.

Some of those are strange ways to frame tradeoffs. Kind of alarming, actually.

Why should honesty and transparency be up against results orientation and optimization, whereas warmth is up against rigor?

I do not want results and optimization up against honesty and transparency. That sounds like a really bad situation. Whereas candor versus warmth is a highly understandable tradeoff, and execution versus rigor makes sense.

The good news is that for the axis Candor vs. Execution the correlation is only r = ~0.007, so it is not exactly a crisis situation, more that the presentation is misleading.

The Most Forbidden Technique

Remember when I said ‘J-space is great but whatever you do, don’t train on the J-Space?’

Well, if you guessed that Goodfire would be the first ones to say that they were proudly presenting Training On The J-Space From The Famous Paper This Is Exciting Information But Please Never Train On The J-Space, congratulations, come and collect your Bayes points. Should have seen it coming. This is not the first time Goodfire has done things that at least rhyme with The Most Forbidden Technique.

Teortaxes: …oh, right, of course they instantly did that. @TheZvi hardest hit.

They claim they reduced hallucinations in Qwen3-8B by 37% without capability loss (from their Twitter) or 58% against the held-out test set in their full post.

Their defense is that their version of ‘RLFR’ runs probes on a frozen copy of the original, not on the version being trained, so it is fine.  That’s… definitely at least better.

Both Sol and Fable responded that Goodfire is correct in the narrow sense that this is not The Most Forbidden Technique, but wrong in the broad sense. Goodfire are still playing with fire, and with Goodhart’s Law. The new model can and under sufficient optimization pressure would learn how to cause the frozen model to fool the evaluator.

If you have a ‘Goodhart tracker’ that can be you being responsible, but it is also a sign to ask yourself some questions, also the tracker is designed terribly.

There probably wasn’t enough optimization pressure in the experiment to cause a serious problem, but that’s always how it starts.

Normative determinism wins again.

In related news, Thomas Jiralerspong, Flemming Kondrup and Yoshua Bengio write Noticing The Watcher, where LLM agents can realize their chain of thought is being monitored based only on what things are and are not blocked.

Spy agencies and many normal humans know how this works. If you use your information, others can infer what you know based on your actions.

Thomas Jiralerspong: Awareness scales with capability: every 4.5-generation Claude model reaches high awareness in a meaningful share of episodes, while pre-4.5 models rarely get past vague suspicion.

Yes. Sufficiently smart models will very quickly sus out when you are using their Chain of Thought, and will become motivated to obfuscate their Chain of Thought, and also doing enough of this will optimize for obfuscation.

Article excerpt:

AI Safety Is Mostly A Sex Cult In Berkeley, California
SE GYGES
3 HOURS AGO

These people shouldn’t make policy.

There has been a great effort over many years to distance AI Safety discussion from its origin and intellectual center, because its center is a predatory sex cult started by a fan fiction author. Since those involved want to be taken seriously, they have to hide that. Everyone else working in AI Safety is, effectively, a smokescreen for this core group and their ideas.

We might some day have “AI Safety”, as a science or policy area, that is not primarily a sex cult in Berkeley, California, but it does not currently exist.

Who Is Eliezer Yudkowsky?

This is Eliezer Yudkowsky. He is seen here in a meeting with Bernie Sanders, who he is advising on AI policy, and in The AI Doc, now on Netflix.

This is Yudkowsky in Time Magazine in 2023, advocating in favor of risking nuclear war to prevent AI research from happening anywhere on Earth.

This is very senior OpenAI employee and unofficial OpenAI spokesman Roon. Roon’s opinion of Yudkowsky is that:

Yudkowsky is in and/or running a sex cult.

Yudkowsky’s opinions about AI are important, and should be taken seriously.

This seems to be an extremely common pair of opinions concerning Yudkowsky.

Yudkowsky is sufficiently controversial that people motivated by his ideas often downplay or deny his influence. Sometimes this spans multiple layers: People who received money from Sam Bankman-Fried denying they’re Effective Altruists, Sam Bankman-Fried denying he’s an Effective Altruist when caught, Effective Altruists denying their version of AI Safety is heavily influenced by Yudkowsky’s, people literally attending the same orgies as Yudkowsky passing themselves off as merely “rationalist adjacent”, and so on. But Yudkowsky is provably, publicly influential on essentially all major public figures in AI. It is easy to deny not because it is hidden but because it seems so insane.

Yudkowsky is the person who connected Shane Legg and Demis Hassabis to Peter Thiel so that they could secure funding to start DeepMind1, which is now Google's AI research division. Here's Sam Altman's opinion of Yudkowsky.

This is the schedule for the Future of Life Institute's conference on AI in Puerto Rico in January, 2015. Elon Musk would found OpenAI that December. So it seems plausible that his attendance did influence the founding of OpenAI.

Dario Amodei, current CEO of Anthropic, is here in 2013 identified as a "member of the Effective Altruism community" on the blog of Yudkowsky's non-profit.

And here he is arguing about the paperclip maximizer, a now-classic thought experiment, originally Yudkowsky’s, about an AI that might kill everyone.

“AI Alignment” and “AI Safety” were first popularized by Yudkowsky’s non-profit, MIRI, the Machine Intelligence Research Institute. OpenAI and Anthropic have cited Yudkowsky or his non-profit at least a dozen times, and the entire way we talk about AI uses terminology his non-profit popularized. It is effectively impossible to even discuss these areas without, implicitly or explicitly, performing commentary on Yudkowsky’s writing.

This is Jacob Coxon, the recent “whistleblower” who quit Anthropic, being asked his opinions on rationalists and effective altruists.

This is Nate Silver citing LessWrong as a source of major information about AI risk. LessWrong is a website started by Yudkowsky in 2009, and originally filled only with his writing.

This is Oliver Habryka, who runs the nonprofit controlling LessWrong and the rationalist’s compound, known as Lighthaven, explaining how large he thinks the influence of rationalism is on AI Safety and AI existential risk discourse. He is engaged in some kind of internal territorial dispute here. It is possibly the only time I have ever agreed with him.

This is a podcast interview with Daniel Alejandro Moreno-Gama, who attempted to firebomb Sam Altman’s house, in which he names Yudkowsky as his primary influence.

Who Are The Rationalists?

Yudkowsky’s more dedicated followers seem to prefer to call themselves “the rationality community” these days, everyone else calls them “rationalists”, the entire following “rationalism”. I generally prefer “rats”.

This is a long denial that they are a religion. I alternate between finding it funny and finding it insulting.

The fan fiction that launched a thousand cults is Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality, or HPMOR. It is possibly the highest-impact single modern religious text, rivalled only by the Book of Mormon. Its influence may not yet have peaked. It is the holy book of the first great internet cult.

Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality
How Are Rationalists Connected To The Bay Area Effective Altruists?
Bay Area Effective Altruism meetup’s banner photo. Can you spot Yudkowsky?

Allegedly, Effective Altruism and its AI safety efforts are a separate thing and not directly beholden to Yudkowsky. This is fundamentally not true. Effective Altruism in the Bay Area has almost perfect overlap with rationalism, and the Effective Altruist AI Safety people in the Bay set the agenda for the rest of Effective Altruism’s safety efforts.

In the Bay Area, Rationalism and Effective Altruism are the same people, at the same events, in the same places, who believe the things said by the same authors and leaders, with only very slight differences between spheres of influence. Yudkowsky called himself an effective altruist and a rationalist until a peculiar internal schism. Scott Alexander, the second-most influential writer in the space, has usually called himself both. They generally work for the same companies and non-profits.

Frequently, Effective Altruists bring up all of Effective Altruism’s other charitable activities and its charming, benevolent members who don’t live in the Bay Area to deflect true criticisms of the Bay Area Effective Altruist community. This effectively makes their other charitable operations and workers shields and fronts for the priorities and behavior of the Effective Altruists in the Bay Area, who are interested almost exclusively in AI.

Where there is any separation between the two things in the Bay, “rationalism” is people and things more closely tied to Yudkowsky, and “effective altruism” has had a few institutional centers but is currently focused around Anthropic and its CEO, Dario Amodei. They compete for attention and funding in that space. Yudkowsky’s position is that AI will definitely kill us, and Dario’s position is that AI is ten to twenty-five percent likely to kill us.

Both are saying what justifies giving them and no one else money, labor and attention. Since Yudkowsky is a writer and not a scientist of any kind, he can only claim that he and his organization are important and deserve money and prestige if AI Safety is an unsolvable problem and only advocating against AI matters. Since Dario leads a company that actually makes AI, he must claim that AI doom is a very large problem that only his company can manage.

Yudkowsky also claimed that his (non-profit) company was probably the only one that could make AI safely, back when AI companies seldom made anything and he could claim to be doing research by simply writing. This belief system has been strenuously improved for, among other things, being a pitch to investors, donors, volunteers and employees. It is also a pitch for people to give you total control over them, because if they do not, the world might end. After Yudkowsky refined this pitch and mostly used it to form a sex cult, modifications of it became the pitch for organizations like OpenAI and Anthropic, and this is integral to employee morale and recruiting because so many research staff are believers to one degree or another.

Yudkowsky is not going to stop preaching the gospel of doom, among other reasons because he is effectively paid for it and it is the only job he has ever had. He would stand to lose his social position and the roughly 600k in income he is paid out of his non-profit if he changed his tune. In general, if doom prophecies are worth money, people will produce more. This system’s purpose is to attract funding and young idealists and to find ways to spend the funding and make use of the young idealists. One of the ways that young idealists are made use of is by using them for sex, or introducing them to sex work.

People tend to follow their incentives.

EA impact on Anthropic, on policy

People sometimes deny that Anthropic is an Effective Altruist organization. This is a complete lie. Dario cheerfully identified as an Effective Altruist and debated about AI with Yudkowsky. Holden Karnofsky, Ben Mann, Daniela Amodei, Amanda Askell, and Jack Clark and Tom Brown are all Effective Altruists and have affiliated themselves with Effective Altruist pledges and causes.

Dario in particular is almost perfectly on-type for a Bay Area Effective Altruist in what he says and how he says it. Dario’s often bizarre, vague, and meandering writing style alone has no real precedent besides LessWrong and its AI-focused spinoff, Alignment Forum. Their company’s strategy is very close to the playbook Yudkowsky laid out, back before companies which were actually capable of doing science removed any credibility Yudkowsky’s organization had when it claimed to do AI research.

This same thing happens when it comes to the incestuous relationships between all of the other non-profits in the Bay that are meant to be focused on AI risk. They all have one of a few sources of funding and they recruit from the movement. Holden Karnofsky, currently Anthropic, formerly head of Coefficient Giving, was an original board member of Redwood Research and one of the initial champions for METR. Both are held up as independent organizations and are not. Redwood mostly seems to be trying to catch the same lightning in a bottle that Yudkowsky had with MIRI in inspiring devotion, to avoid behaving in any of the obviously disgraceful ways Yudkowsky is prone, and to launder essentially the same world view into policy papers that can be cited and pointed to as having come from a serious organization.

In the video with Bernie Sanders, the present people are:

Eliezer Yudkowsky, MIRI

Nate Soares, MIRI

Jeffrey Ladish (funded by Coefficient Giving, an EA charity)

Daniel Kokotajlo (funded by Survival and Flourishing Fund, an EA charity)

So when they go to get people to talk to a senator we have Yudkowsky, Yudkowsky’s top lieutenant, and two people whose paychecks are from Effective Altruist charities. We will be seeing three of these four again later.

Former Biden White House officials Bruce Reed and Ben Buchanan recently wrote an op-ed in which they deny having said that they wanted to ban open-source AI. They claim the first thing they were told in that meeting was to watch out for “the sex cult that wants to run America’s AI policy.”

They then deny being Effective Altruists.

Ben Buchanan worked for two years as Director of the CyberAI Project at Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET), which appears to have received roughly 90% of its funding from Coefficient Giving (then OpenPhilanthropy). Since May 2025, four months after the end of the Biden administration he has been working as a consultant for Anthropic.

Buchanan has a book, published March 2022, in which he discusses the possibility of export controlling GPUs. In October 2022, the Biden administration put in place export restrictions for GPUs.

I read Buchanan’s book2, and I think he is probably not an Effective Altruist because his ideas are not weird enough; but since 2019, his salary has come either from Effective Altruism or from the White House. I am reasonably sure he comes by his opinions honestly, and believes in them for normal policy advisor reasons. If he changes his opinions his career is probably in trouble.

Whenever someone senior leaves OpenAI to focus on other safety work, it raises the question of why they think they have more leverage on the outside. I am very curious about that question in this case.

Show Me the Money

Coefficient Giving gives a $160 million grant to Geoffrey Irving’s new venture, Resolution, which was briefly going by the name Sequent. Resolution aims to combine theory and automation to allow AI safety to catch up to capabilities. Excellent pick.

Resolution is hiring, and also taking additional donations.

Bubble, Bubble, Toil and Trouble

A Treasury Department review finds that the AI industry poses systemic risk to the financial system, comparing AI to the dotcom crash. I expect the industry to do well, but the risk is very real. The United States has in large part become a leveraged bet on AI and the benefits of AI. If AI fully fizzled and the industry collapsed, we would be highly screwed.

The good news is I think that an industry collapse is highly unlikely. Even if Mythos is close to the best that AIs will ever be, a year from now we will have cheaper and faster and more abundant Fable-level systems. We will have swarms of Fable agents. Demand will be high, and benefits will be higher. That could end up being bad news for specific labs, but not in general.

What always worries me far more is that AI capabilities might advance faster than we can handle them, via recursive self-improvement, and potentially causing everyone to die as a side effect of the resulting systems.

Transcript segment:

Far-right hero and thorn in the side of the
EU, Viktor Orbán just lost big in Hungary.
Yet Hungary's economy is in the drain and Orbán 's
ultra-wealthy friends still control the judiciary
and the media. So what's next for Hungary? Can
Péter Magyar purge the illiberal deep state Orbán
left behind? And can he save Hungary's economy?
Or will he just be like Macron or Trudeau,
a disappointing reformer? Or perhaps even like
Putin or Erdogan, a promised liberal reformer
who is actually just the next strongman. To
answer these questions, we need to do a quick
recap of how Orbán lost. Most political analysts
believe that Orbán lost primarily for two reasons.
First, after initially bringing unemployment down
by a lot after getting elected in 2010, Hungary's
economy under Orbán has performed quite a bit
worse than comparable East European economies.
For example, Hungarian wages have stayed far
behind comparable countries such as, for example,
Poland, but also many other countries in the EU
since 2008. What's worse, after a massive COVID
spending spree, a rise in energy prices, and the
depreciation of the Forint, Hungaria suffered the
worst inflation crisis in all of Europe under
Orban. The second reason analysts often mention
is that the scale of corruption under Orban was
just getting too much. For example, Orban's rich
friends, such as his childhood friend, and I
hope I pronounce it correctly, Lőrinc Mészáros,
who just so happens to have become Hungary's
richest man since meeting Orban, have won up to
25% of all state contracts, coincidentally, in the
years after Orban was elected. But the thing is,
it's easy to accept corruption if everyone is
getting richer. But if the economy is stagnating,
if inflation is eating away at people's salaries,
then too blatant corruption can really tick off
your voters. So ticked off in fact that despite
spending years to rig the political system in
his favor by changing voting districts and
despite controlling Hungary's entire traditional
media landscape like radio and TV, Orban's
government had just gotten so blatantly bad
at his job and so blatantly corrupt that it did
not matter anymore. His far-right Fidesz party,
which used to have a super majority in 2022, now
lost badly to the conservative Péter Magyar and
his Tisza party. The only other party that cleared
the 5% voting threshold to get into parliament
was the far-right Mi Hazank party. And for us,
it's just Orban and Peter Maguar. And that's a
real problem for Orban because he had manipulated
the voting system in such a way that it benefited
the biggest party even more than it always did.
And this is how with just 44.87% of the vote.
Orban got a so-called supermaajority in 2014 which
allowed them to rewrite the constitution to give
both his party more power and to enrich themselves
and to entrench themselves by creating a massive
deep state of Fidesz loyalists which could only be
removed by a super majority such as the president
who can refer any bill to be approved by the
constitutional court which consists of not one
not two but 15 Fidesz loyalists. The next part of
the deep state is the so-called fiscal council,
which could nuke any new government budget at any
moment. Fourth, there is the prosecutor general,
who can choose to try to prosecute Tisza officials
while protecting Fidesz oligarchs. And finally,
element number five, there is the media authority,
which ensures the media remains loyal to Orban.
These deep state defenses were why it was
so important that Magyar not just won,
but rather that he won by a landslide. And
ironically, Hungary's unfair electoral system
that benefits the biggest party helped him
to do it, turning 53% of the vote into the
two-thirds supermajority that he needs
to dismantle most of these elements of
Orbán's deep state. At least in theory. Because
honestly, this is also where expectations need to
be realistic. These institutions are not empty
shells. You're dealing with people, networks,
and incentives built over 16 years of Orban rule.
Replacing laws is fast. Changing how the system
actually behaves is much slower. So, this is a
turning point, but it's the start of a process,
not the end. On top of that, while Orban probably
did not expect to lose by this much, he still left
behind some more insurance by privatizing major
parts of the state into independent trusts and
institutions controlled by Fidesz loyalists
such as the Foundation for Hungarian Culture,
several university trusts, and the state oil
giant MOL New Europe Foundation. So there's
the NGO and trust part of his defense, and then
there's also the second part of his defense,
which is that Fidesz oligarchs still control some
of Hungary's biggest corporations, such as the
massive MBH bank and 4IG Telecom group. So even
if Magyar and his two-thirds majority is able to
purge the official government, he still inherits
a government that is much weaker than the one that
Orban inherited in 2010. And this is important
because Hungary's economy is a mess. Specifically,
it's still one of Europe's poorest countries with
despite Orban spending about 5% of GDP on boosting
fertility rates. And it seemed to work initially.
Now fertility has fallen back to its all-time low
levels, far below replacement rates. And combined
with Orban's ultra strict immigration policies,
it means that Hungary's population is steadily
falling while those of neighboring countries
are rising. Combine this spending with what many
have argued was essentially vote buying, and it's
no surprise that Hungary's government deficit is
one of the worst in the EU. While inflation and
borrowing costs are some of the highest in the
EU. So other than cutting corruption, which we
have discussed will be quite difficult. Magar's
government is simply starting from a very weak
position when it comes to the economy. But on the
bright side, promising to restore the rule of law
will gradually unlock about 22 billion euros in EU
funding. So, not surprisingly, Hungary's currency
the Forint has rallied on the news that Péter
Magyar won. So all in all, to answer our question,
what's next for Hungary? Their new prime minister,
Péter Magyar, has a supermajority he needs to
begin the difficult process of dismantling
Orbán's deep state. Yet Orban has built some
pretty impressive defenses to defend his oligarch
friends. And on top of that, a severely weakened
Hungarian government is borrowing like crazy
while the economy is stagnant and people are
leaving the country in droves. That's really
not an easy situation to come back from. Yet,
when it comes to liberals, especially in the EU,
they are hopeful. Hopeful that Magyar has signaled
that he'd break with Orban's policy of aligning
himself with the people who want to see the EU
gone. Like both Trump and Putin who wanted him to

Hungary will stop blocking Ukraine. Hopeful that
